pr_body:
# Objective

- Make people stop believing that commands are applied immediately (hopefully).
- Close #5913.
- Alternative to #5930.

## Solution

I added the clause “to perform impactful changes to the `World`” to the first line to subliminally help the reader accept the fact that some operations cannot be performed immediately without messing up everything.

Then I explicitely said that applying a command requires exclusive `World` access, and finally I proceeded to show when these commands are automatically applied.

I also added a brief paragraph about how commands can be applied manually, if they want.

---

### Further possibilities

If you agree, we can also change the text of the method documentation (in a separate PR) to stress about enqueueing an action instead of just performing it. For example, in `Commands::spawn`:

> Creates a new `Entity`

would be changed to something like:

> Issues a `Command` to spawn a new `Entity`

This may even have a greater effect, since when typing in an IDE, the docs of the method pop up and the programmer can read them on the fly.

issue_context.title: Commands is poorly communicated to new users
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

I've had to tell new users that things done through Commands don't apply until the end of the stage tens of times. I'm fine with that, but it does indicate to me that there's something about the Commands documentation or API that is misleading to new users, and I'm not sure if it'd take a rethinking of how the Commands API is named, or just more obvious documentation of this, but I thought I'd bring it up because I do see it as a general communication issue with Bevy right now.
comments:
If only those users checked the documentation...

https://docs.rs/bevy_ecs/0.8.1/bevy_ecs/system/struct.Commands.html

> If only those users checked the documentation...
> 
> https://docs.rs/bevy_ecs/0.8.1/bevy_ecs/system/struct.Commands.html

Regardless we have to work with the world we have and not the world we wish we had 😅

Interpreting those docs correctly requires an understanding of the engine that users often do not have yet when this hits them.

This seems like a book problem to me.

> let's just rename `Commands` to `DeferredCommands` smile #5930

I can already hear people asking where is `InstantCommands` 😆

review_comments:
> I think we need to explicitly say somewhere that calling a function on Commands will only add a Command to the queue.

The best place to do that is the methods' descriptions themselves. But I want to split that to a different PR, since I noted that it is best to keep docs PRs very tight-scoped.

The methods should say that yes, but I think it's important to also say it in the struct doc because there's clearly some confusion about this. It feels like the current doc is pretty much already saying that, just not explicitly.

I still think that it is redundant since the PR already states

> all queued commands are automatically applied in sequence only after each system in a stage has completed.

which is clear enough IMO. If people have wrong expectations about the behavior of the methods, it's because the docs for the methods are wrong.
